content:
Ricky Springfield claims he killed a man during his trip to Vietnam to perform for US troops in the late 60s.

The Australian musician detailed the shocking experience during an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience this week.

The "Jessie's Girl" singer said on the podcast: "During Vietnam you could go over there and tour — it was absolutely crazy. We were there for about four months. I was like, 'Great, we can make some money.' You know? And of course, we didn't make any money at all."

Money became irrelevant at one point of the tour when survival became the priority, with the group staying alongside a bunch of soldiers when they were attacked.

Springfield said: "It was just like the movies. The radio came on and uh, 'We see some activity over there, confirm if friendlies.' They said, 'No, there are no friendlies over there.' So they said, 'Hey do you want to drop a few mortars on them?' That's the John Wayne moment, you know. I mean, I was a young kid, I had no idea what I was doing. I was like, 'Yeah, let me have a go.'"

"I dropped the mortars, about five or six, and I could have lost my hand at any point during that," Springfield said. He added: "The next morning they came back and said one of them got a Viet Cong."

Springfield, who was just 18 at the time, said that was when the gravity of what he had done truly hit him.

"The hardest thing for me to deal with is that, uh, I dropped that mortar on somebody. It was just... something I brought back that I couldn't find a place for," he said.

When host Joe Rogan asked how long the incident has weighed on him, Springfield replied: "It's still there."

"For me it's hard to face the fact that I ended a life, even though it was a long time ago, even though it was a war, even though I wasn't really involved, even though I didn't really know what I was doing," he said, adding that the truth of what happened "weighs heavy" every time he thinks about it.
